*"Fallin’"* is a classic pop song recorded by **Connie Francis**, one of the most successful female vocalists of the late 1950s and early 1960s. Here’s everything you need to know about the song:

---

### **1. Release & Chart Performance**
- **Release Date:** October 1958 (as a single, B-side to *"You’re Gonna Miss Me"*)
- **Label:** MGM Records (catalog #K12745)
- **Chart Performance:**
  - Peaked at **#30 on the *Billboard* Hot 100** (December 1958).
  - Did not chart as strongly as some of Francis’ other hits (e.g., *"Who’s Sorry Now?"*, *"Lipstick on Your Collar"*), but became a fan favorite.
  - Also charted in the UK, reaching **#25** on the *New Musical Express* chart.

---

### **2. Songwriters & Composition**
- **Written by:** **Neil Sedaka** and **Howard Greenfield**
  - This was one of the first major hits for the young songwriting duo, who later became legends in pop music (responsible for hits like *"Calendar Girl"*, *"Breaking Up Is Hard to Do"*, and *"Love Will Keep Us Together"*).
  - Sedaka was just **19 years old** when he co-wrote *"Fallin’"* (his first big success).
- **Musical Style:**
  - A **doo-wop-influenced pop ballad** with a lush orchestral arrangement.
  - Features a **dramatic, ascending melody** in the chorus, showcasing Francis’ powerful, emotive vocals.
  - The lyrics describe the pain of falling in love with someone who doesn’t feel the same way.

---

### **3. Connie Francis’ Version**
- **Vocal Style:**
  - Francis delivers the song with **raw emotion**, a hallmark of her early recordings.
  - Her **belting, operatic-influenced voice** contrasts with the more restrained doo-wop style of the era.
- **Arrangement:**
  - Produced by **Morty Kraft** (who worked on many of Francis’ hits).
  - Features a **lush string section**, **piano**, and **backing vocals** (likely by The Ray Charles Singers or similar groups).
  - The **bridge** ("*I try to fight it, but I know it’s no use*") is a standout moment, showcasing her dynamic range.
- **B-Side:**
  - The flip side was *"You’re Gonna Miss Me"*, another Sedaka-Greenfield composition, which also charted (#71 on *Billboard*).

---

### **4. Legacy & Influence**
- **Early Career Boost for Sedaka & Greenfield:**
  - *"Fallin’"* was one of the first songs to establish Sedaka and Greenfield as hitmakers. Sedaka later recorded his own version in 1960 (though it was less successful).
- **Connie Francis’ Signature Sound:**
  - The song exemplifies Francis’ ability to blend **pop, rock ‘n’ roll, and traditional Italian influences** (she was of Italian descent).
  - It’s often included in **retrospective collections** of her work, such as *"The Very Best of Connie Francis"* (1996).
- **Cultural Impact:**
  - While not as iconic as *"Stupid Cupid"* or *"Where the Boys Are"*, *"Fallin’"* is a **cult favorite** among fans of **1950s/60s pop and doo-wop**.
  - It has been **covered by other artists** (see below) and remains a **nostalgic favorite** in oldies radio playlists.

---

### **5. Cover Versions**
- **Neil Sedaka (1960):**
  - Sedaka recorded his own version for his album *"Neil Sedaka Sings Little Devil and His Other Hits"* (1960). His rendition is **softer and more piano-driven** than Francis’.
- **The Four Seasons (1964):**
  - Featured on their album *"Dawn (Go Away) and 11 Other Great Songs"*, with **Frankie Valli** on lead vocals. Their version is **more upbeat and harmonized**.
- **Other Artists:**
  - **Lesley Gore** (1960s demo, unreleased until later compilations).
  - **The Chiffons** (1960s, though not officially released).
  - **Modern covers** by artists like **Dusty Springfield** (live performances) and **nostalgia acts**.

---

### **6. Fun Facts & Trivia**
- **Sedaka’s First Hit:**
  - *"Fallin’"* was the **first song Sedaka and Greenfield wrote together** that became a hit, paving the way for their future success.
- **Connie’s Italian Connection:**
  - Francis later recorded an **Italian version** of the song titled *"Cadere"* (1960), which was popular in Italy.
- **Film & TV Appearances:**
  - The song has appeared in **nostalgic films and TV shows**, including:
    - *"The Marvelous Mrs. Maisel"* (Season 2, 2018) – featured in a 1950s-themed scene.
    - *"Mad Men"* (background music in some episodes).
- **Connie’s Personal Favorite?**
  - In interviews, Francis has mentioned that while she loved all her hits, *"Fallin’"* was one of the songs that **showcased her vocal range the best**.

---

### **7. Where to Hear It**
- **Albums:**
  - *"Connie Francis Sings Italian Favorites"* (1959) – includes the original version.
  - *"The Very Best of Connie Francis"* (1996, Rhino Records).
  - *"Connie Francis: The Complete MGM Recordings"* (2017, Real Gone Music).
- **Streaming:**
  - Available on **Spotify, Apple Music, YouTube, and Amazon Music**.
- **Radio:**
  - Still played on **oldies and doo-wop radio stations** (e.g., SiriusXM’s *50s on 5*).

---

### **8. Lyrics (Key Excerpt)**
*(Chorus)*
> *"Fallin’, fallin’ in love with you,*
> *I never thought that I would do.*
> *Fallin’, fallin’ in love with you,*
> *But now I know that it’s true!"*

*(Bridge)*
> *"I try to fight it, but I know it’s no use,*
> *I’m just a fool for your charms.*
> *I try to hide it, but I can’t refuse,*
> *I’m fallin’ right into your arms!"*

---

### **9. Why It Stands Out**
- **Emotional Depth:** Unlike some of Francis’ more upbeat hits, *"Fallin’"* is a **heartbreak ballad** that highlights her dramatic vocal ability.
- **Historical Significance:** It marks the **beginning of Neil Sedaka’s songwriting career** and is a great example of **1950s pop craftsmanship**.
- **Timeless Appeal:** The song’s **melancholic yet beautiful melody** has kept it relevant for over **60 years**.

---

### **10. Similar Songs by Connie Francis**
If you like *"Fallin’"*, check out these other Connie Francis ballads:
- *"My Happiness"* (1958) – A cover of the 1948 hit, showcasing her softer side.
- *"Among My Souvenirs"* (1959) – A dramatic, orchestral ballad.
- *"Mama"* (1960) – A tearjerker about a mother’s love.
- *"Breakin’ in a Brand New Broken Heart"* (1961) – Another Sedaka-Greenfield collaboration.

---

### **Final Thoughts**
*"Fallin’"* may not be Connie Francis’ **biggest hit**, but it’s a **gem** in her discography—a **perfect blend of doo-wop, pop, and raw emotion**. It’s a must-listen for fans of **1950s/60s vocal pop**, **Neil Sedaka’s early work**, and **Connie Francis’ powerful voice**.
